title: Monday Morning Quarterback (on Sunday)
date_line: Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026. College weekend review: Tuesday through Saturday (Oct. 27-31), graded. Then next college weekend.

paragraphs: This is college football Week 9 against the spread, graded, and it was a weekend for bad nerves. Kansas State vs Colorado went to overtime and split the tickets down the middle on the last snap. Kansas vs TCU landed dead on the spread. Western Michigan vs Bowling Green and North Dakota State vs UTEP each missed the number by half a point, Boise State vs Texas State flipped a 25-point halftime lead into a one-point win and a lost cover, and the over/under board broke hearts from Durham to Fresno. Florida vs Georgia and Ohio State vs USC went the wrong way early and stayed there.

All 56 games on the card from Tuesday through Saturday are graded below against the line printed on the card at kickoff, with ESPN finals and play-by-play. A push counts as neither a hit nor a miss. The heartbreakers go first, then the escapes, then the rest of Saturday, then the weeknight games.

Follow The Money and In The Trenches sit out when a game doesn't fit them: Follow The Money had no side in 48 games and no total in 35, and In The Trenches had no side in 34 games and no total in 51. Those games aren't graded for them. Letdown Watch made no picks this week.

Card line: Kansas State −1.5, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had Kansas State −1.5 and the Over, projecting Kansas State 28, Colorado 23. Final: Kansas State 24, Colorado 27. Colorado won by 3 in overtime, and the teams scored 51 points.

This one put Kansas State −1.5 holders through every emotion a point and a half can produce. Colorado's Young broke a 22-yard touchdown run early in the fourth to make it 21-14 Colorado, and K-State kicker Luis Rodriguez then missed from 43 yards with 6:52 to play. K-State tickets looked dead. Then Blake Barnett found Garrett Oakley from 8 yards out with 2 seconds on the clock, the kick tied it at 21, and the Over 47.5 crowd sat at 42 points hoping for overtime just to stay alive.

Overtime. K-State got the ball first and Rodriguez hit from 25 yards. 24-21, K-State −1.5 covering by a point and a half, and the total at 45, still 2.5 short of the Over. Colorado's turn. Wilson hit Williams from 11 yards out on the final snap of the night. Colorado 27, K-State 24. The same walkoff touchdown that ripped up every K-State −1.5 ticket cashed the Over 47.5 by 3.5. One throw, two verdicts, and half the room yelling for the opposite reason as the other half.
Called it: Follow The Money on Colorado +1.5, covered by 4.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 47.5, cleared it by 3.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on Kansas State −1.5, missed by 4.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the total; In The Trenches on the total.
Card line: TCU −6, total 46.5. The Cover Writer's card had Kansas +6 and the Under, projecting TCU 25, Kansas 20. Final: Kansas 16, TCU 22. TCU won by 6, and the teams scored 38 points.

Kansas +6 looked like the safest cash on the board for most of the afternoon. Cole Ballard hit Cam Pickett for a 29-yard touchdown and a 13-0 lead. Then TCU's Carroll picked off Ballard and went 60 yards the other way, and Theus ran 28 yards to flip it to 14-13 TCU. TCU even had a 94-yard interception return touchdown wiped out by its own interference flag at 7:32 of the fourth, and Kansas made it hurt with a 27-yard field goal for a 16-14 lead with 4:59 left.

At that moment Kansas +6 was covering by 8 and winning outright. Craig marched TCU downfield and ran 17 yards for the go-ahead touchdown with 1:11 left, and TCU converted the two-point try with Dwyer. 22-16. Six points. Exactly the number. Kansas got into TCU territory in the final 20 seconds, a Kansas holding flag shoved it back to the TCU 49, and Ballard's final heave was broken up. The Under 46.5 never sweated and finished 8.5 under, but every Kansas +6 ticket got its money back and not a dime more.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Under 46.5, stayed under by 8.5 points.
Push: The Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on Kansas +6, landed exactly on the number. Next Man Up on TCU −6, landed exactly on the number.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the total.

Card line: Western Michigan −13.5, total 44.5. The Cover Writer's card had Western Michigan −13.5 and the Over, projecting Western Michigan 31, Bowling Green 14. Final: Bowling Green 10, Western Michigan 23. Western Michigan won by 13, and the teams scored 33 points.

Western Michigan −13.5 holders needed 14 points of daylight and spent the whole fourth quarter one score short of it. Cabana's 82-yard touchdown run had the Broncos rolling in the first quarter, and a 50-yard field goal made it 20-10 with 13:27 left. Western Michigan picked off Bowling Green at the BG 22 with 1:58 to go and had a short field to go get the cover.

The drive stalled. A 36-yard field goal came off the board on a Western Michigan holding flag, and the re-kick from 46 went through with 15 seconds left. 23-10. Thirteen points. Half a point short of 13.5. Bowling Green threw another interception with 12 seconds left just to twist it, and the Over 44.5 had been dead for hours, stuck at 33.
Called it: Next Man Up on the Under 44.5, stayed under by 11.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on Western Michigan −13.5, missed by 0.5 points. The Cover Writer and The Formula on the Over 44.5, fell 11.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

Card line: North Dakota State −24.5, total 42.5. The Cover Writer's card had North Dakota State −24.5 and the Over, projecting North Dakota State 37, UTEP 10. Final: UTEP 7, North Dakota State 31. North Dakota State won by 24, and the teams scored 38 points.

North Dakota State −24.5 holders sat at 17-7 from late in the third quarter until 1:45 to play, 14.5 points short and praying. Moore III's 57-yard touchdown run in the first quarter was the only UTEP score of the day, so the defense held up its end. Then the late surge. Hayes ran it in from a yard out with 1:45 left, and 39 seconds later Marion Moore scooped a fumble and went 46 yards for another touchdown.

31-7. Twenty-four points. The number was 24.5. And the Over 42.5 needed one more UTEP touchdown to get to 45: Moore III drove UTEP to midfield and his last heave fell incomplete at the NDSU 4 with one second left. Two tickets, both half a breath from home, both missed.
Called it: The Formula, Follow The Money and In The Trenches on UTEP +24.5, covered by 0.5 points. Follow The Money on the Under 42.5, stayed under by 4.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and Next Man Up on North Dakota State −24.5, missed by 0.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula, Next Man Up and In The Trenches on the Over 42.5, fell 4.5 points short.

Card line: Boise State −11.5, total 64.5. The Cover Writer's card had Boise State −11.5 and the Under, projecting Boise State 38, Texas State 26. Final: Texas State 45, Boise State 46. Boise State won by 1, and the teams scored 91 points.

Boise State −11.5 was a laugher at halftime. Madsen threw a 12-yard touchdown with 4 seconds left in the half and Boise led 28-3, covering by 13.5. Under 64.5 holders were sitting at 31 points with a full half to play. Then Texas State scored 36 straight points. Jackson ran 35 yards for one touchdown, hit Sparks for 44 yards to take the lead, and Bradley picked off Madsen and went 20 yards for a touchdown at 8:58 of the fourth. 39-28 Texas State.

Boise came back under Max Cutforth, failing on three two-point tries along the way. Texas State's Sample took a short throw 72 yards for a 45-40 lead, and Akeem Wright's 18-yard catch with 2:40 left won it for Boise, 46-45. Boise won the game by one and lost the cover by 10.5, and the Under 64.5 lost by 26.5 in a second half that produced 60 points.
Called it: Next Man Up and Follow The Money on the Over 64.5, cleared it by 26.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on Boise State −11.5, missed by 10.5 points. The Cover Writer and The Formula on the Under 64.5, went over by 26.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

Card line: Air Force −2.5, total 53.5. The Cover Writer's card had UConn +2.5 and the Over, projecting Air Force 29, UConn 27. Final: UConn 26, Air Force 35. Air Force won by 9, and the teams scored 61 points.

UConn +2.5 was a live ticket until the last four minutes. The Huskies missed an extra point after Alex Godavitarne's 55-yard touchdown catch late in the third, then Kenji Christian broke a 46-yard touchdown run with 14:46 left to make it 28-26 Air Force. The two-point try failed, but down two, UConn +2.5 was covering by half a point and the total had already climbed over 53.5.

Air Force ground the clock and Kemper Hodges punched in a 1-yard run with 3:09 left. 35-26. Cover gone, by 6.5 points for the card and by 7.5 for Follow The Money at +1.5. Those two missed conversions loomed over the whole fourth quarter. The Over 53.5 was the consolation prize, cleared by 7.5.
Called it: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 53.5, cleared it by 7.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on UConn +2.5, missed by 6.5 points. Follow The Money on UConn +1.5, missed by 7.5 points.
No pick: Follow The Money on the total; In The Trenches on the side or the total.

Card line: San Diego State −2.5, total 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had Washington State +2.5 and the Over, projecting San Diego State 27, Washington State 25. Final: Washington State 20, San Diego State 26. San Diego State won by 6, and the teams scored 46 points.

Both Washington State tickets died on the same final drive. Stevens missed a 53-yard field goal late in the third. San Diego State's Ford caught a 2-yard touchdown at 9:47, two-point try failed, and it was 26-14. Washington State drove inside the 5 on a 43-yard catch that ended in a fumble Washington State recovered at the SDSU 4, and Eshelman ran it in from 2 yards out at 6:55, but Stevens' extra point failed.

26-20, total 46. Washington State +2.5 needed a field goal. The Over 48.5 needed a field goal. Same three points for both tickets. Washington State got the ball back and Eshelman's fourth-down throw was broken up at the SDSU 26 with 38 seconds left. Turnover on downs. Two tickets, one incompletion, and a missed extra point haunting all of it.
Called it: Next Man Up on San Diego State −2.5, covered by 3.5 points. Next Man Up on the Under 48.5, stayed under by 2.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and In The Trenches on Washington State +2.5, missed by 3.5 points. The Cover Writer and The Formula on the Over 48.5, fell 2.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the total.

Card line: Ohio State −6.5, total 51.5. The Cover Writer's card had Ohio State −6.5 and the Over, projecting Ohio State 34, USC 23. Final: Ohio State 18, USC 30. USC won by 12, and the teams scored 48 points.

Ohio State −6.5 was gone by the third quarter at 27-9. The Over 51.5 was not. Fahey hit Smith from a yard out with 2:12 left, but the two-point try failed: 45 points. Chittenden's 32-yard field goal at 1:46: 48 points.

Ohio State drove right back to the USC doorstep and kept throwing into the end zone. The fourth-down throw fell incomplete with 36 seconds left, a turnover on downs. A touchdown there puts the total at 54 and cashes the Over. Instead it finished at 48, short by 3.5, and Ohio State −6.5 missed by 18.5 for good measure.
Called it: In The Trenches on USC +6.5, covered by 18.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on Ohio State −6.5, missed by 18.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 51.5, fell 3.5 points short.
No pick: Follow The Money on the side or the total; In The Trenches on the total.

Card line: Duke −7, total 47.5. The Cover Writer's card had Duke −7 and the Under, projecting Duke 29, Boston College 18. Final: Boston College 2, Duke 47. Duke won by 45, and the teams scored 49 points.

Duke −7 was cashed by halftime. The Under 47.5 was the sweat, and it was cruel. Boston College's only points of the day came in the first quarter, when Davis returned a Duke extra-point try for a defensive two-point conversion. Remember those 2 points.

Strange's 41-yard field goal at 12:02 of the fourth made it 44-2, a total of 46 with a running clock and 1.5 points to spare. Then Strange lined up again from 24 yards with 2:58 left. Good. 47-2, a total of 49, Under 47.5 dead by a point and a half. Take away the defensive conversion and the Under cashes with room.

Card line: BYU −16.5, total 48.5. The Cover Writer's card had BYU −16.5 and the Over, projecting BYU 37, Arizona State 19. Final: Arizona State 20, BYU 27. BYU won by 7, and the teams scored 47 points.

BYU −16.5 never got close, with Arizona State tying it 17-17 in the third. The Over 48.5 is where the pain lived. Arizona State had a 26-yard field goal blocked at the end of the first quarter, and Moa's 1-yard run with 2:09 left made it 27-17, a total of 44.

Smith drilled a 44-yard field goal with 57 seconds left: 47 points, needing one more field goal. Arizona State's onside kick went 8 yards and died. BYU then went for it on fourth down with 3 seconds left instead of kicking, and the throw fell incomplete. 47. Over 48.5 short by 1.5, and that first-quarter blocked kick was exactly the margin.
Called it: The Formula on Arizona State +16.5, covered by 9.5 points.
Missed: The Cover Writer and Next Man Up on BYU −16.5, missed by 9.5 points. The Cover Writer, The Formula and Next Man Up on the Over 48.5, fell 1.5 points short.

Gramatica's 33-yard field goal with 1:36 left made it 40, and that's where it ended. Over 42.5 short by 2.5, with UAB's own kicker leaving six points on the grass.

Card line: Indiana −20.5, total 41.5. The Cover Writer's card had Indiana −20.5 and the Over, projecting Indiana 34, Minnesota 11. Final: Minnesota 16, Indiana 23. Indiana won by 7 in overtime, and the teams scored 39 points.

Indiana −20.5 was dead long before overtime. The Over 41.5 was the ticket with a pulse, and Indiana's own kicking game kept choking it. Radicic had a 52-yard field goal blocked and missed from 31 yards in the second quarter.

Minnesota's Drzewiecki hit from 60 with 19 seconds left, Paddy McAteer answered from 60 yards at the gun, and it went to overtime at 32 total, 9.5 short. Wilson hit Becker for a 25-yard touchdown in overtime, and Minnesota's answer died on a sack and a turnover on downs. 39 points. Short by 2.5, with six Indiana points left on the field in the first half.

Card line: Louisiana Tech −5.5, total 57.5. The Cover Writer's card had South Alabama +5.5 and the Over, projecting Louisiana Tech 33, South Alabama 30. Final: Louisiana Tech 35, South Alabama 20. Louisiana Tech won by 15, and the teams scored 55 points.

South Alabama +5.5 never got closer than the number after Louisiana Tech pulled away in the third, and Watkins' 4-yard catch at 0:39 of the third made it 35-20. That was the last score of the day. The Over 57.5 sat at 55 for a full quarter, needing one field goal.

South Alabama threw into the end zone on fourth down at 6:39 and turned it over on downs. Louisiana Tech went for it on fourth down in South Alabama territory at 2:39 instead of kicking, and that failed too. Then South Alabama was picked off at the Louisiana Tech 5 with 1:40 left. A scoreless fourth quarter, three trips near the end zone, zero points, and the Over 57.5 lost by 2.5.

Auburn +13.5 died early in the fourth as Chambliss threw two touchdowns in less than three minutes, the second a 28-yarder to Fields for 38-15. The Under 57.5 was still alive at 53 with 3:27 left, and with a 23-point lead the obvious move was to run out the clock.

Fresno State +5.5 was cashed by the end of the third, with Freeman's 31-yard catch making it 38-16. The Under 57.5 was the sweat, sitting at 54 deep into the fourth. Fresno's Watanabe even missed a 44-yard field goal at 12:26, and Oregon State turned it over on downs at 9:21 and again at 7:02.

Then garbage time bit. Atkinson hit Olsen for a 9-yard touchdown with 1:45 left. 38-22. Total 60. The two-point try failed and didn't matter. Under 57.5 dead by 2.5 on a touchdown that changed nobody's evening except the bettors'.

Southern Miss led 27-7 after three quarters, and Over 55.5 holders were at 34 needing 22 points in a quarter. UL Monroe got two touchdowns: Armenta's 1-yard run and his 2-yard throw to Trujillo at 6:47. 27-21, total 48, and suddenly Southern Miss −3.5 was a sweat too, up only six.

Wilder broke a 32-yard touchdown run with 1:52 left, and Sanders converted the two-point try. 35-21. Southern Miss −3.5 cashed by 10.5. Total 56. Over 55.5 by half a point, and the two-point conversion made it happen. A kick makes it 55 and the Over loses.

Barnett's 64-yard touchdown run put Illinois up 17-14 with 14:50 left. O'Haire tied it with a 46-yard field goal at 10:16. Illinois −2.5 holders now needed a win by three, and only a field goal at the end would do it.

Illinois drove deep, then knelt at the Maryland 7 with 24 seconds left to set up the kick. Ethan Moczulski from 26 yards as time expired. 20-17, Illinois −2.5 by half a point, on a kneel-down and a chip shot. The Over 54.5 had no part in any of it and finished at 37.

Card line: SMU −10, total 58.5. The Cover Writer's card had Syracuse +10 and the Under, projecting SMU 32, Syracuse 26. Final: SMU 27, Syracuse 30. Syracuse won by 3, and the teams scored 57 points.

Syracuse +10 was never in real trouble, since SMU's biggest lead was seven. The Under 58.5 was a heart attack. A safety at 12:07 of the fourth cut it to 20-19, SMU down a point. Kendrick Raphael's 13-yard run and a two-point conversion made it 27-20 SMU at 9:04, and Tripp Woody's 26-yard field goal cut it to 27-23 at 5:26. Total 50, 8.5 points of room.

Steve Angeli hit Noah Meyers from 2 yards out with 17 seconds left: 30-27 Syracuse, total 57, 1.5 points of room. Then SMU's final snap: a short completion, a fumble, and Syracuse's Geter scooping it and returning it 13 yards before the play died. A Syracuse scoop-and-score there kills the Under at the gun. It didn't happen. Syracuse +10 won outright, and the Under 58.5 cashed by 1.5.

hits.heading: Part 1, continued: The week's W-L and smack talk

paragraphs: The Cover Writer went 26-29-1 against the spread and 20-36 on totals. Saturday alone was 23-23-1 on sides and 16-31 on totals, which is a coin flip on sides and a dumpster fire on totals. The Duke Under died on two points Boston College scored on a returned extra-point try. The Indiana Over died with six Indiana points left on the field. The Kansas State side died on the final throw of overtime. Every one of those tickets was a field goal or a two-point play from home, and the card gets graded on results, not near misses.

The Formula went 27-28-1 on sides and 22-34 on totals. Saturday ran 22-24-1 on sides and 19-28 on totals, and The Formula sat right next to the Cover Writer on the Kansas State and Western Michigan heartbreaks, then turned around and cashed UTEP +24.5 by half a point while the Cover Writer was swallowing North Dakota State −24.5.

Next Man Up went 26-29-1 on sides and 21-35 on totals, with Saturday at 24-22-1 on sides and 18-29 on totals. Next Man Up took Ole Miss −13.5, San Diego State −2.5 and the Over in Boise State vs Texas State, all against the Cover Writer, and cashed all three. Expect to hear about it.

Follow The Money went 5-3 on sides and 11-10 on totals, Saturday at 5-1 on sides and 7-6 on totals. Follow The Money was the only voice on Colorado +1.5 and got paid on the final snap of overtime while the rest of the desk tore up K-State tickets, then added UTEP +24.5 and the Under 42.5 in the same game for good measure.

In The Trenches went 6-15-1 on sides and 1-4 on totals, Saturday at 5-12-1 on sides and 1-1 on totals. Temple +6, Northwestern +3.5 and Washington State +2.5 missed by 2, 4.5 and 3.5 points, and Kansas State −1.5 went down on the last throw of overtime. Close doesn't cash at the window.
Letdown Watch made no picks this week, so Letdown Watch is the only handicapper here who didn't lose a ticket.
